title: Recovery from bounded-above truncations
statement:
For every $E\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the canonical morphism

$$
\operatorname{hocolim}_{N\to+\infty}\tau_{\le N}E\longrightarrow E
$$

is an isomorphism, where the homotopy colimit is that of
[def-kun-truncations].

proof.text: In the derived category of etale Lambda-module sheaves, form the natural-number diagram of the canonical upper truncations and their inclusions into E. Compatibility of truncation inclusions implies that the sum a of the inclusions annihilates the specified telescope endomorphism t=1-shift. Exactness of Hom(-,E) on the given distinguished triangle gives c:H→E with p c=a, hence all required coprojection equations.

For any abelian category, a compatible cocone whose maps are isomorphisms from some index N onward is colimiting: use the inverse of its Nth map to define descent and use compatibility on either side of N for the factorization equations. Consequently, if B is the coproduct and t=1-shift, the sum a of the cocone maps is a cokernel of t. Indeed, a map out of B annihilates t exactly when its restrictions to the summands form a compatible cocone. This argument is the proved private stableTelescopeCokernel construction.

Homology preserves countable coproducts in the derived category of etale module sheaves by the proved source-library DerivedCategory.preservesColimitsOfShape_homologyFunctor. The sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian; AB5 implies exact countable coproducts. Apply [lem-kun-sequential-telescope-mono] after each homology functor: H^r(t) is monic in every degree. The long exact homology sequence of the given triangle then makes H^r(p) a cokernel of H^r(t). The standard truncation triangle implies H^r(truncLEι(n)) is invertible for r≤n: the complementary truncGE(n+1) has zero homology in degrees r-1 and r. Take N=r.toNat. The previous step shows H^r(a) is also a cokernel of H^r(t). The equality H^r(p) H^r(c)=H^r(a) identifies H^r(c) with the canonical map between these cokernels, so it is invertible. Mathlib DerivedCategory.isIso_iff now proves c invertible.
